title: Commission adopts €1.8 billion EIC work programme for 2027
dek: The last EIC programme under Horizon Europe reshapes Pathfinder and Transition, sets four Accelerator cut-offs and opens Pathfinder Open on 25 November.
key_facts: EIC Work Programme 2027, the final one under Horizon Europe
€428 million Open, €150 million Challenges; cut-offs 20 January, 17 March, 1 September and 4 November 2027
€166 million Open, €82 million Challenges; Open call opens 25 November 2026, stage 1 deadline 25 February 2027
€290 million STEP Scale Up; €100 million STEP Defence Scale Up, deadline 1 June 2027
body: The European Commission has adopted the 2027 work programme of the European Innovation Council, with the EIC announcing €1.8 billion in funding for deep tech innovators. The document states that this is the last EIC work programme under Horizon Europe.

The largest single line is the EIC Accelerator, with an indicative €428 million for open applications and €150 million for four challenge topics covering ocean observation, climate-neutral and smart cities, fusion power plant technologies and carbon removal. Full proposals can be submitted at four cut-offs in 2027. The programme also refines the evaluation criteria, introduces a reserve list and simplifies resubmission.

Two early-stage schemes change shape. Pathfinder Open moves to a two-stage evaluation that includes interviews, while Transition becomes a single-beneficiary instrument, although affiliated entities and subcontractors remain possible, and adds a video pitch.

For later-stage companies, STEP Scale Up offers equity of €10 million to €30 million across four batches, and STEP Defence Scale Up offers the same range in a single batch closing on 1 June 2027. The Scaleup Europe Fund, for equity above €30 million, has an indicative €400 million. Pathfinder, Transition and the Advanced Innovation Challenges remain civil-only; dual-use activities can be funded under the Accelerator, STEP Scale Up and the Scaleup Europe Fund.
why: This is the last chance to plan around EIC rules under the current framework programme, so applicants should check their scheme choice now rather than rely on last year's approach. University-led Transition consortia are the most affected: the project needs one clear owner, and partners must be reorganised as affiliated entities or subcontractors. Pathfinder Open teams should prepare for interviews, not only a written proposal. Dual-use companies need to pick their route carefully, because the wrong scheme could rule out defence-related work. Dates can move, so confirm them on the official call pages before committing resources.
